network.overall_strategy: This network prioritizes the best-supported arginine-specific chemistry rather than forcing a single origin scenario. The core de novo module is the UV-driven surface cyanosulfidic sequence: HCN plus acetylene gives acrylonitrile, ammonia gives beta-aminopropionitrile, HS-/UV gives beta-aminopropionaldehyde, cyanamide diverts that branch into a guanidinated C3 intermediate, and further HCN/H2S homologation yields the experimentally supported arginine alpha-aminonitrile. Free arginine is then released only after a separate hydrolysis step, because that endpoint is chemically expected but less directly demonstrated than the aminonitrile precursor. A second, shorter late-stage module captures the strong chemistry of ornithine guanidination by cyanamide. Contested direct Fischer-Tropsch-type arginine assignments and unresolved glutamate-to-ornithine protometabolic bridges are not used as core target-forming edges.

reactions.name: Cu(I)-mediated HCN-acetylene coupling to acrylonitrile

conditions.other: UV-exposed anoxic surface pool; staged cyanide delivery; local cyanide concentration by evaporation or ferrocyanide release is favored

reactions.mechanism: Cu(I)-activated coupling of cyanide-derived carbon with acetylene gives the C3 nitrile acrylonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. identified acrylonitrile as the entry point to the Arg/Pro branch from HCN and acetylene under Cu-mediated cyanosulfidic conditions. A subaerial surface setting is favored because UV is available and cyanide can be locally concentrated and stored in ferrocyanide-bearing basins before release, though that geochemical sequencing is demanding (Patel et al., 2015; Toner and Catling, 2019; Ranjan and Sasselov, 2017).

reactions.name: Ammonia addition to acrylonitrile

conditions.other: Anoxic aqueous pool with dissolved NH3/NH4+; no molecular oxygen

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia adds across the activated alkene/nitrile system to form beta-aminopropionitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Ammonia addition to acrylonitrile to give beta-aminopropionitrile is a core early step of the Patel arginine branch and is chemically straightforward in anoxic water. Among Arg-specific steps, this is relatively well supported experimentally (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Cu-accelerated HS-/UV conversion of beta-aminopropionitrile to beta-aminopropionaldehyde

conditions.other: UV irradiation; anoxic HS-/H2S photoredox; sulfur output is a formal S(0)/polysulfide sink

reactions.mechanism: HS-/UV photoreduction converts the nitrile to an aldehyde-equivalent, with water participation and net ammonia release.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. used sulfide-driven photochemistry to access beta-aminopropionaldehyde from beta-aminopropionitrile. The node is written as the balanced net transformation consuming water and sulfide and releasing NH3 plus elemental sulfur/polysulfide. Copper is treated here as a kinetic accelerator rather than an absolute requirement. Surface sulfide supply is a real geochemical constraint, so this step is strongest in locally sulfidic surface waters (Patel et al., 2015; Ranjan et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Aldehyde-stage cyanamide guanidination

conditions.other: Residual cyanamide present immediately after aldehyde generation; anoxic, concentrated surface pool

reactions.mechanism: Cyanamide traps the aminoaldehyde and yields a guanidinated aldehyde-equivalent pool represented here by an open-chain network surrogate.
reactions.reasoning: The literature favors aldehyde-stage interception by cyanamide over direct guanidination of the aminonitrile. Patel et al. found that residual cyanamide rapidly trapped the photogenerated aminoaldehyde and diverted chemistry toward the arginine branch; this node intentionally represents that equilibrating trapped pool as an open-chain guanidinated aldehyde equivalent rather than claiming a single uniquely isolated species (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Direct cyanamide guanidination of beta-aminopropionitrile

conditions.other: Concentrated cyanamide; competing unreacted starting material persists

reactions.mechanism: The terminal amine attacks cyanamide to give a guanidino-functionalized nitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Direct cyanamide guanidination of beta-aminopropionitrile is chemically possible but was relatively inefficient in the Patel study, which left appreciable starting material and cyanamide in the mixture. It is therefore retained only as a lower-flux alternative branch and not as the preferred route (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Speculative HS-/UV conversion of guanidino nitrile to guanidinated aldehyde equivalent

conditions.other: UV irradiation with dissolved sulfide; included as a low-confidence continuation of the direct guanidination branch

reactions.mechanism: HS-/UV photoreduction and hydrolytic ammonia loss convert the guanidino nitrile into a guanidinated aldehyde-equivalent.
reactions.reasoning: This step is speculative. The provided literature supports inefficient direct guanidination of beta-aminopropionitrile, but it does not clearly establish this guanidino-nitrile-to-aldehyde sequence as a separately characterized arginine-specific step. It is included because any productive direct nitrile-stage branch must still reach an aldehyde-equivalent before further homologation, and the Patel HS-/UV chemistry makes such a transformation chemically plausible even if less well supported than the aldehyde-first route (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Cu-accelerated Patel homologation to arginine alpha-aminonitrile

conditions.other: UV-driven staged HCN/HS- additions; net stoichiometry implies 2 HCN and 2 H2S; anoxic surface pool-to-pool sequence

reactions.mechanism: Sequential cyanohydrin formation, thioamide chemistry, and UV/H2S-driven homologation extend the guanidinated C3 branch to the C6 arginine alpha-aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: This reaction deliberately compresses several Patel substeps into one balanced network edge; the stoichiometry implies two HCN and two H2S equivalents even though each reactant appears once in the graph. It stands for cyanohydrin formation, thioamide formation, UV/H2S deoxygenation, and final homologation to the experimentally characterized arginine alpha-aminonitrile precursor. Patel et al. supported the alpha-aminonitrile itself, not a quantified isolated free-arginine endpoint. Copper is included here as an accelerator, not as a universally mandatory reagent (Patel et al., 2015; Ranjan et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Surface hydrolysis of arginine alpha-aminonitrile

conditions.other: Prolonged aqueous residence or wet-dry rehydration in geothermal surface pools; balanced form requires 2 H2O

reactions.mechanism: Aqueous hydrolysis of the alpha-aminonitrile gives the amino acid and releases ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Hydrolysis of an alpha-aminonitrile to the corresponding amino acid is the expected Strecker endpoint; the balanced form of this node requires two waters and releases NH3. For arginine specifically, Patel et al. established the aminonitrile precursor rather than free arginine as the headline product, so this step is chemically plausible but less directly demonstrated than formation of mol_013 (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Mineral-interface hydrolysis of arginine alpha-aminonitrile

conditions.other: Post-photochemical transfer to concentrated prebiotic pools or mineral interfaces; balanced form requires 2 H2O

reactions.mechanism: Slow aqueous nitrile hydrolysis proceeds after the photochemical construction stage, allowing environmental succession between modules.
reactions.reasoning: The same hydrolysis chemistry could occur after transfer of the aminonitrile into concentrated prebiotic pools or mineral interfaces, separating UV construction from slower nitrile hydrolysis. This environmental handoff is plausible but not directly validated for arginine, so the step is explicitly more speculative than the formation of the aminonitrile precursor itself (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Sulfide-only HS-/UV conversion of beta-aminopropionitrile to beta-aminopropionaldehyde

conditions.other: UV irradiation with dissolved HS-/H2S but no explicit copper accelerator; sulfur output is a formal S(0)/polysulfide sink

reactions.mechanism: Sulfide photoreduction alone converts the nitrile to the aldehyde-equivalent with hydrolytic ammonia release.
reactions.reasoning: A Cu-free sulfide-photoredox variant is included because Patel's broader cyanosulfidic system does not require copper for every reduction, although copper can accelerate photoredox turnover. This version is chemically defensible but likely slower and more sensitive to local sulfur availability than rxn_003 (Patel et al., 2015; Ranjan et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Sulfide-only Patel homologation to arginine alpha-aminonitrile

conditions.other: UV-driven staged HCN/HS- additions without explicit copper acceleration; net stoichiometry implies 2 HCN and 2 H2S

reactions.mechanism: The same HCN/thioamide/homologation logic as rxn_007 operates without copper acceleration.
reactions.reasoning: This is the Cu-free analogue of rxn_007. It represents the same Patel-type HCN/H2S homologation logic but without invoking copper acceleration, which is chemically plausible in parts of the cyanosulfidic network yet likely kinetically less favorable. As with rxn_007, the secure literature endpoint is the arginine alpha-aminonitrile rather than free arginine (Patel et al., 2015; Ranjan et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Cyanamide guanidination of ornithine

conditions.other: Concentrated cyanamide in mildly basic to neutral prebiotic pool; no mineral catalyst required

reactions.mechanism: The terminal delta-amine of ornithine attacks the electrophilic carbon of cyanamide and tautomerizes to the guanidino group of arginine.
reactions.reasoning: Terminal amine guanidination is the chemically shortest late-stage route from a C5 skeleton to arginine. Longo et al. showed complete Orn->Arg conversion for peptide-bound ornithine under aqueous guanidination conditions, and cyanamide is a plausible simple prebiotic guanidinating reagent from classic chemical-evolution work. However, a fully naturalistic free-ornithine-plus-cyanamide environmental synthesis of free arginine remains underconstrained, and ornithine supply is itself a bottleneck despite abiotic ornithine evidence from volcanic discharge chemistry (Longo et al., 2020; Steinman et al., 1964; Johnson et al., 2008).

pathways.name: Preferred Patel branch with surface hydrolysis
pathways.description: Most evidence-weighted de novo route: Cu-mediated entry chemistry, Cu-accelerated HS-/UV aldehyde formation, aldehyde-stage cyanamide interception, Cu-accelerated homologation to the alpha-aminonitrile, then surface hydrolysis.

pathways.name: Preferred Patel branch with post-transfer hydrolysis
pathways.description: Same chemically preferred de novo construction as P1, but free arginine appears only after transfer of the alpha-aminonitrile to a concentrated prebiotic pool or mineral interface for hydrolysis.

pathways.name: Minimal-copper aldehyde-generation variant
pathways.description: Aldehyde-stage guanidination is retained, but the nitrile-to-aldehyde step is run by sulfide photochemistry without explicit copper acceleration.

pathways.name: Minimal-copper aldehyde-generation with post-transfer hydrolysis
pathways.description: As in P3, but hydrolysis of the alpha-aminonitrile is deferred to a later concentrated pool or mineral-interface stage.

pathways.name: Cu-free late homologation variant
pathways.description: Uses the preferred aldehyde-stage cyanamide capture but omits copper acceleration in the C3-to-C6 Patel homologation sequence.

pathways.name: Cu-free late homologation with post-transfer hydrolysis
pathways.description: Same as P5 through the alpha-aminonitrile, but free arginine is released in a later pool/interface hydrolysis step.

pathways.name: Direct nitrile-stage guanidination branch
pathways.description: Lower-confidence alternative in which cyanamide first guanidinates beta-aminopropionitrile, the guanidino nitrile is then reduced to the aldehyde-equivalent, and Cu-accelerated homologation delivers the alpha-aminonitrile.

pathways.name: Direct nitrile-stage guanidination with post-transfer hydrolysis
pathways.description: Same lower-confidence direct guanidination branch as P7, but the alpha-aminonitrile is hydrolyzed in a later concentrated pool or mineral-interface setting.

pathways.name: Lowest-confidence cyanosulfidic branch
pathways.description: Combines the direct nitrile-stage guanidination shortcut with Cu-free late homologation; chemically possible but weaker than aldehyde-first Patel logic.

pathways.name: Ornithine-first late-stage guanidination
pathways.description: Chemically shortest shortcut to arginine: pre-existing ornithine is guanidinated by cyanamide in water. This is a valid competing module, but not a complete de novo route because ornithine provenance remains the main bottleneck.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the most literature-aligned branch: it follows the Patel surface route through beta-aminopropionaldehyde and aldehyde-stage cyanamide trapping to the arginine alpha-aminonitrile, then hydrolyzes to arginine. Main issues are that rxn_007 collapses several published homologation and thioamide substeps and should explicitly use 2 HCN + 2 H2S, and rxn_008 needs 2 H2O.

Correct stoichiometry: rxn_007 needs 2 HCN + 2 H2S; rxn_008 needs 2 H2O.
Add explicit UV, Cu, pH, and staged-addition conditions.

evaluation.network_feedback: Network validity is strong: the graph is connected, molecule IDs are used consistently, and the RDKit check reports no UNBALANCED reactions; four reactions are simply shorthand with omitted coefficients. Literature alignment is also strong because the network centers the Patel arginine alpha-aminonitrile chemistry, treats free arginine as a later hydrolysis product rather than overstating the 2015 endpoint, includes ornithine guanidination only as a late-stage module, and does not rely on contested Fischer-Tropsch or unresolved glutamate-to-ornithine claims. The main weaknesses are chemical granularity and environment specification: rxn_007 and rxn_011 compress several Patel substeps, mol_012 is an aggregate intermediate, rxn_006 is only speculative, and the 'Biochemical' environment for rxn_009 and rxn_012 is too vague. Correct the explicit stoichiometry in the shorthand reactions: rxn_007 and rxn_011 need 2 HCN + 2 H2S, while rxn_008 and rxn_009 need 2 H2O. Overall this is a good, literature-aware network, but it falls short of approval because the free-arginine endpoint is still inferred via hydrolysis and several edges remain under-specified.
